horizon.reason: a free plate's continuum reference is a table of tabulated values (Narita/Leissa), not a formula over all modes, so a horizon exists only over the tabulated set (plan section 5).

this domain is staircased onto the grid, so the error being measured is the SHAPE, not the scheme: the continuum reference is a frequency for a different outline, and a cents comparison would mix a geometry error into a dispersion one. That needs a geometry-convergence study rather than this primitive (plan section 5).
